item.text: The main remaining feature-specific risk is whether the LRU cache’s serialized/cloned decoder has the same ordering issue as LFU under more varied eviction sequences. I’m stress-testing LRU clone/decode synchronization across cache sizes and random access patterns to separate a general cache-transfer defect from the already-confirmed LFU-only defect.

item.text:
The audit now contains 13 confirmed findings. The latest high-impact result is in the UniCache path:

- **LFU clone causes silent value corruption.** [lfu_cache.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/omnipaxos/src/unicache/lfu_cache.rs:18) copies cache entries to a follower but not their frequency state, so leader and follower evict differently. A decoded cache hit for `"A"` produced `"C"`. Reproduced by [audit_lfu_clone.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/omnipaxos/tests/audit_lfu_clone.rs). The equivalent LRU control and 160 randomized LRU runs passed, isolating the defect to LFU.

Other newly confirmed defects:

- Persistent atomic writes leak partially applied operations after errors; a later unrelated transaction committed an entry from the failed transaction.
- A reconfigure request made before leader election remains buffered and is never forwarded after `AcceptSync`.
- `UniCacheEntry` fails to compile as documented because generated code requires undocumented imports, and its serde derivation is controlled by the downstream crate’s feature name rather than `omnipaxos/serde`.

All reproduction sources, commands, and outputs are preserved under `work/`. The complete evidence is in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/report.md).
